div.p: This tool edits the detector response function (DRF) currently in use, or builds one from scratch when opened with a blank detector (the "Make without data..." button of the "Create Detector Response Function" tool, or when no detector is loaded). Nothing is changed until you press Use; Cancel discards the edits.

How the detector is modeled for sources close to the detector or off its axis. "Flat Disk" is the traditional model: the crystal is a disk of the stated diameter, and only the source distance matters. "Geometry Modeled" describes the crystal (shape, material, dimensions, dead layer, endcap layers) and uses that description to evaluate the response for any source position:

ul.li: No MC support (from measured curve): instant. The DRF's own measured efficiency (or its curve) is transferred to other positions through the ray-traced geometry. Accurate on axis and mildly off-axis; the reported uncertainty grows off-axis and very close in.

Quick MC and Full MC: run a Monte-Carlo characterization of the geometry (minutes), which is then corrected ("grounded") to the DRF's measured efficiency points when it has them. Full MC also models the response well off-axis and at contact.

div.p: Press Generate Response after editing the geometry or the anchor points; the response is marked stale until you do.
Fits, or lets you enter, the peak-width (FWHM) equation of the detector from the peaks in the current spectrum.

The efficiency data the DRF is pinned to. Depending on the DRF this is a table of measured points (energy, efficiency, statistical and certificate uncertainties, source and distance), the coefficients of the efficiency equation with their covariance, or a formula. Edit a value to change the response; the uncertainties you enter here are what the analysis tools propagate into their activity uncertainties. For a DRF made by the "Create Detector Response Function" tool the points are the measured peaks, and each keeps its own source distance.
